title: WOW: Refactor switch-case into functions, fields into structs
description:
This is preparation for my work on https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/11398 which adds more fields and complexity of parsing, requiring a slight refactor.

I wanted to get this merged ahead of the actual work since it's a relatively large refactor and it's easier to consider it in isolation. This entire PR can be squashed if the maintainers feel like it spams up the commit history, I just separated it out to ease review.

For verification the captures from https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/11398 should be used.

notes.body: hf_ is reserved for header fields plese consider another name.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3039/diffs?diff_id=188389094&start_sha=b35b1692a35181557c2d514f9ff2a0bc33a40f09#8f371561938f68b5807a571e5cb210bbf5e05ed3_187_127)

What the advantage of use a struct ? 
it is not on wireshark style code (and not sure if all check tools will be happy)

It's to group all the related fields together, since many of the fields only appear in one packet.

I could not find anything about in the [developer README](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/doc/README.developer) that disallowed this.

If you want me to change it back I can just revert the commits and sort the fields under comment headers or something?

Sorry, I'll push a fix. The whitespace in this file in general seems a little weird.

Part 5 of the [developer docs](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/doc/README.developer) mention 4 spaces being the standard but the file uses tabs + manual spaces in some areas for example to align ending brackets in enums.

I wanted to convert it to 4 spaces but I wasn't sure what the correct protocol for doing so was. Is it OK if I just run it through `cat -t 4` to convert tabs to 4 spaces?

packet-wow.c(612): warning C4700: uninitialized local variable 'wow_realms_tree' used
That's a false positive. The var is being passed to a function which initializes the var on line 304 and uses it on line 309 and later.
Why do you need to pass the variable ? is never use after (or before)

Ah, I get what you mean.

I assumed that the `dissect_wow_pdu` function was special and that `proto_tree` items needed to be declared there. I'll push a fix.
I've pushed a fix, if you need further changes let me know. :)
